source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha (BCPP / Prague Stock Exchange) — Novinky / News announcement service
why_relevant: Central publication venue where BCPP posts exchange notices and issuer-related announcements (admissions, suspensions, exclusions from trading, index changes, corporate events) with an exchange-side timestamp that is independent of the issuer's own IR page. Searchable with Czech diacritics, AND/OR operators and a From/To date range, and filterable by source (BCPP vs ČTK newswire). Individual items have stable slug URLs, e.g. /novinky/vylouceni-emise-avast-z-obchodovani, /novinky/pozastaveni-a-vylouceni-emise-z-obchodovani, /novinky/novy-index-px-start, /novinky/jarni-start-day-2025. English mirror at /en/news.

source_name: BCPP issuer detail pages (per-ISIN) — Přehled / O společnosti / Novinky / Reporty / Prezentace a Research / Korporátní kalendář
why_relevant: Per-issuer hub keyed by ISIN. Confirmed tabs: Přehled (Overview), Obchodní data (Tick Data), Historická data, O společnosti (Company Profile — registered address, IR website link, business description), Novinky (News). Additional per-issuer sections observed: Profil, Reporty, Prezentace a Research, Korporátní kalendář, dividend history, warrants. For the CZ banking cell this is the exchange-side landing page for KOMERČNÍ BANKA (CZ0008019106), MONETA MONEY BANK (CZ0008040318) and ERSTE GROUP BANK (AT0000652011), and for payments-adjacent issuers SAB FINANCE (CZ0009009940) and WAG PAYMENT SOLUTIONS / Eurowag (GB00BLGXWY71).

source_name: BCPP Prime Market share list (Prime Market — akcie)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of the strictest-disclosure regulated segment. As observed it carries 12 issues, of which three are banks with full CZ/EU disclosure duty: ERSTE GROUP BANK (AT0000652011), KOMERČNÍ BANKA (CZ0008019106), MONETA MONEY BANK (CZ0008040318); VIG (AT0000908504) adds insurance/bancassurance exposure. This list is the cheapest reliable way to know which CZ-listed banks currently carry Prime-level disclosure duty and to detect additions/removals.

source_name: BCPP Standard Market share list — includes SAB FINANCE (FX/cross-border payments)
why_relevant: Regulated market for other equity issues. As observed it carries 8 issues including SAB FINANCE a.s. (CZ0009009940) — a licensed Czech FX/payment-services provider and the closest thing on the regulated CZ market to a listed pure payments company — plus RMS MEZZANINE (CS0008416251), a financial/investment vehicle. This makes the Standard Market list the main pointer to non-bank financial issuers with statutory disclosure duty.

source_name: BCPP Free Market share list (Volný trh) — foreign bank and payment issuers dual-listed in Prague
why_relevant: Unregulated segment used mainly for dual listings; it is where the Prague venue carries the largest cluster of banking/payments names: WAG PAYMENT SOLUTIONS (Eurowag, GB00BLGXWY71 — commercial road-transport payments), DEUTSCHE BANK (DE0005140008), OTP BANK (HU0000061726), PKO BANK POLSKI (PLPKO0000016), RBI / Raiffeisen Bank International (AT0000606306), UNIQA INSURANCE (AT0000821103), ATS (AT0000969985). Useful as a CEE-peer watchlist anchored to a Czech venue, and the only Prague-listed pure payments name found in this scan.

source_name: BCPP START Market issuer list (trh START)
why_relevant: The SME/growth segment (MTF) open only to Czech and Slovak companies — the venue where a small Czech fintech would most plausibly list, and the reason this cell exists as a fintech early-warning tripwire. Observed roster: BEZVAVLASY, EMAN (CZ0009009718 — IT/software house that builds banking and mobility apps), FILLAMENTUM, FIXED.ZONE, HARDWARIO, M&T 1997, M2C, MMCITÉ, PILULKA LÉKÁRNY, PRABOS PLUS. No pure payments/fintech issuer was present at scan time, but the list must be diffed because admission requires only a CEO decision, so new names can appear between quarterly auctions.

source_name: BCPP debt securities — Financial Sector bond list (dluhopisy, finanční sektor)
why_relevant: Highest-value single page in this cell for banking coverage: it names the Czech banks that carry exchange disclosure duty through bond listings even when they have no listed equity. Observed issues include HZL MONETA 4,83/27 (CZ0002009020) and HZL MONETA 4,97/26 (CZ0002009012), HZL RB CRR 1,00/30 (Raiffeisenbank, CZ0002007057), HZL UCB 3,04/28 (UniCredit Bank, CZ0002003114), J&T BANKA VAR/34 (CZ0003709339), MONETA MB VAR/29 and VAR/30, UCB 0,00/28 and 0,00/29. 'HZL' = hypoteční zástavní list (covered/mortgage bond) — a direct signal on bank funding structure.

source_name: BCPP debt securities — Other Bonds segment (perpetuals: J&T BANKA, J&T FINANCE GROUP)
why_relevant: Small but analytically dense segment: observed entries are J&T BK 7,00% perpetual (CZ0003707275) and J&T FG 7,50% perpetual (CZ0003527657) — i.e. the Prague venue is where a privately held Czech banking group's capital instruments become publicly observable. Perpetual/AT1-style listings are one of the few public windows into non-listed CZ bank capital positions.

source_name: ftp.pse.cz — Annual.rep: BCPP archive of issuer annual reports (výroční zprávy) including ESEF XHTML
why_relevant: Open, directory-listable bulk archive of annual reports filed with the exchange by listed issuers, organised in year folders (2012 through 2020/2021 folders observed) plus loose files at root; ~130+ company reports observed, in PDF, ZIP and XHTML (ESEF/iXBRL) form, uploaded April–August of the following year. This is the exchange's own copy of the filing — the artefact that survives when an issuer's IR site is later re-organised, and it includes financial-sector filers. Machine-readable ESEF XHTML makes structured extraction of bank financials feasible.

source_name: ftp.pse.cz — Semiannual.rep: BCPP archive of issuer half-year reports (pololetní zprávy)
why_relevant: Companion half-year filing archive, year folders 2012–2021 observed plus loose files, ~150+ distinct company reports in PDF/ZIP/XLSX/7Z/DOCX. Issuer codes visible in the listing include financial names (ICBA, RZBCL — Raiffeisenbank, CSPOL, TRIREL) alongside industrials, i.e. it covers bank/financial filers whose equity is not listed but whose bonds are. Half-year reports carry the interim P&L and balance-sheet detail that annual reports only confirm six months later.

source_name: ftp.pse.cz root — BCPP bulk data server (Info.bas, Statist.dta, Cdcp.dta, Results.*, Member.dta, Tom.dta)
why_relevant: The exchange's undocumented bulk-file backbone and the best pointer inside this cell. Root listing observed: Annual.rep, Cdcp.dta, Info.bas, Issuers.dta, IssuersCDCP.dta, Member.dta, Results.act, Results.ak, Results.old, Semiannual.rep, Service.dta, Statist.dta, TESTIssuers.dta, TESTresults, Tom.dta, Vestnik.doc, VestnikCDCP.doc, plus Readmecz/Readmeen files. Info.bas contains CEEplus, Cz, Eng, Indexy, News, RTS_27, START, Statistiky and XETRA_T7 subtrees, several with 2025–2026 modification dates, i.e. it is live, not an abandoned archive. Info.bas/Cz holds BCPP's own quarterly and annual reports (vz93–vz15), IFRS financial statements, PX / PX-GLOB / PX-TR / PX-START index series as CSV, index calculation rules, and member trade-volume reports.

source_name: ftp.pse.cz — Issuers.dta (exchange issuer master data feed)
why_relevant: Name and position in the tree strongly suggest a structured issuer master-data feed (the counterpart of Member.dta for members and IssuersCDCP.dta for depository-side issuer records). If accessible it would be the cleanest machine-readable roster of all BCPP issuers with duty status — exactly the pointer this cell is supposed to supply. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a confirmed dataset.

source_name: ftp.pse.cz — Vestnik.doc / VestnikCDCP.doc (Burzovní věstník — Exchange Bulletin archive)
why_relevant: The Burzovní věstník is the exchange's official gazette in which admissions, exclusions, suspensions and issuer notices are formally promulgated — the authoritative, dated record of record for anything that happens to a listed issue. VestnikCDCP.doc is the depository counterpart. Because the gazette is the legal publication venue, it is the strongest evidence when an IR page or a news item is later edited or withdrawn.

source_name: BCPP Event Calendar / Korporátní kalendář (issuer corporate calendar)
why_relevant: Exchange-maintained forward calendar of issuer events — dates of preliminary results and annual reports for the previous financial year, general meetings (valná hromada) at which financial statements are approved, dividend dates. Future events are exportable to Google/Outlook calendars (date only). Historical entries allow download of the related documents, which turns the calendar into a second route into results releases. Directly serves the 'earnings' and 'annual reports' topics for KB, Moneta and Erste on a scheduled, anticipatable basis.

source_name: BCPP Start Day calendar & Start Market information obligations
why_relevant: START Market issuers discharge their disclosure duty largely through 'Start Day' — a twice-yearly event at which issuer representatives present the actual economic situation and business development to investors and analysts. This page carries the Start Day calendar and the associated information-obligation schedule, so it is both a calendar and the definition of what a START fintech would have to disclose and when. Note the fee incentive documented in the Start Market Rules: the annual fee can be reduced to CZK 0 if the issuer commits by 30 November to procure a published analytical report on itself — meaning sponsored equity research exists for these issuers and is a collectable artefact.

source_name: BCPP Rules & Regulations (Burzovní pravidla) — incl. 'Regulation on Fulfilment of Duties and Obligation of Issuers' and Start Market Rules
why_relevant: The normative layer that tells a collector what each issuer MUST publish, in what language, and by when — essential for turning absence-of-a-filing into a signal rather than noise. Key documents captured: 'Regulation - Fulfilment of Duties and Obligation of Issuers' (PSE-Regulation-Fulfilment-of-duties-and-Obligation-of-Issuers.pdf), Part VI Prime Market share admission conditions, Part VII Standard Market, Part VIII bonds on the Official Market, Part IX debt securities on the Regulated Market, Part XIII Free Market Rules, Part XVI Start Market Rules, Part XIV Exchange Fees. Bond issuers must discharge disclosure duty in Czech, Slovak or English; Official Market bond admission requires three years of financial statements.

source_name: BCPP Issuers' Guide and issuer FAQ pages (Nejčastější otázky a odpovědi pro emitenty)
why_relevant: Plain-language exchange explanation of where regulated information actually lands: each issuer keeps an investor section on its own website, and certain documents/notices are additionally published on the BCPP website and on the supervisory authority's website. That three-way split is the operational map for this whole cell. The per-market FAQ pages (Prime / Standard / Free / Start) give the segment-specific version, including the IPO and prospectus-passporting route for dual listings.

source_name: BCPP Official Price List (Kurzovní lístek) and Statistics Files
why_relevant: The official price list is the single page that enumerates every admitted instrument across asset types (shares, bonds, investment funds, structured products) and segments (Prime, Standard, Free, Start) for a chosen date — the most complete roster of who currently carries an admission on the Prague venue, including bank bond issues that never appear on any equity list. The Statistics Files page exposes the machine-friendly download patterns: monthly statistics at http://ftp.pse.cz/Statist.dta/Objemy/Month/monthly-statistics-YYYYMM.pdf and member turnover at http://ftp.pse.cz/Info.bas/Cz/Objemy_obchodu_clenu/YYYY/objYYMM.pdf, plus a 2015–2025 key-data file.

source_name: BCPP Press Centre (Tiskové centrum)
why_relevant: Exchange-side press channel and the human route into the cell: press contact info@pse.cz, +420 221 832 820 / +420 724 504 946, X/Twitter @prazskaburza, plus CEO biography (Petr Koblic, FESE President in 2018) and downloadable logos/press photos with an explicit free-use grant for journalistic, private, educational and scientific purposes. The press office is the correct addressee for access requests on the 401-gated ftp branches and for questions about issuer data licensing.

source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha, a.s. own annual reports (BCPP / PX Group as an issuer and as a market operator)
why_relevant: The exchange's own consolidated annual report is a quantified read on the health of the Czech listing channel itself: listing revenue, market-data revenue (market data licensing was 4.56% of PX Group operational revenue, CZK 35.057 million, with the latest fee change in 2025), member counts, IPO activity. Useful for judging whether the Prague issuer channel is expanding or shrinking as an intelligence surface. BCPP itself has an ISIN (CZ0008042603). Historical series of BCPP annual and quarterly reports sit on the ftp server (vz93–vz15, 1q15–3q16, BCPP_IFRS_2013/2014).

source_name: Wiener Börse — Prague partner-exchange market data & BCPP ownership channel (CEESEG)
why_relevant: BCPP is a ~99.5% subsidiary of Wiener Börse AG within CEE Stock Exchange Group; Prague trading data is disseminated through the Vienna-operated ADH / rapidADH feeds, and Vienna calculates the indices for the group's markets. This is therefore the commercial gateway to real-time and historical Prague issuer/market data, and the place where licensing terms and vendor lists live. Wiener Börse also publishes issuer annual reports and prospectuses for its own market segments, which matters for the Austrian bank issuers cross-listed in Prague (Erste, RBI, VIG, UNIQA).

source_name: Centrální depozitář cenných papírů, a.s. (CDCP) — issuer/ISIN register and Věstník
why_relevant: The Czech CSD assigns ISINs and maintains the central securities register; it contracts directly with issuers whose shares are admitted to BCPP trading, and publishes information on registered securities in its Věstník. It is the identity backbone that lets you join a BCPP ticker to a legal entity, and it captures issuers (including bank bond programmes) before or without an exchange announcement. BCPP's ftp server carries mirrored CDCP branches (Cdcp.dta, IssuersCDCP.dta, VestnikCDCP.doc), confirming an operational data link between the two.

source_name: RM-SYSTÉM, česká burza cenných papírů — Zprávy od emitentů (parallel Czech exchange issuer news)
why_relevant: The second licensed Czech exchange (a market since 1993, an exchange since December 2008), split into an official market and a free market (MTF). It runs its own 'Zprávy od emitentů' issuer-news archive with deep pagination, which sometimes carries Czech issuer notices in a different form or ordering than BCPP and is therefore a genuine cross-check on the Prague issuer channel. Its official market imposes the statutory disclosure and takeover obligations; its MTF explicitly does not, which makes the segment split itself a useful classification signal.

source_name: Kurzy.cz — CZ securities issue/issuer database and issuer-announcement archive
why_relevant: Long-running Czech financial portal that maintains a per-ISIN issue database sourced from the central depository, an issuer index browsable by first letter, and a dated archive of issuer/auction announcements. Because it is a third-party mirror with its own timestamps and its own retention, it is the practical fallback when a BCPP page or an issuer IR page is edited or withdrawn, and its issuer index surfaces bond-only issuers that the BCPP equity lists never show. It also republishes BCPP listing-rule documents.

source_name: BCPP indices — PX, PX-TR, PX-GLOB and PX-START (constituents and CSV series)
why_relevant: Index membership is a compact, rules-based proxy for which issuers matter on the Prague venue, and PX-START is specifically the START-market index — delisting from the exchange triggers immediate removal from PX-START, so index-change notices double as delisting alerts. Banking weight in PX (KB, Moneta, Erste, VIG) makes the index a quick sector-exposure gauge. Historical series and the calculation rulebooks are downloadable as CSV/PDF from the ftp server.

source_name: BCPP 'PX Veřejná nabídka' — public offering platform rules and documentation (START/IPO placement)
why_relevant: The exchange's own primary-placement mechanism for the START segment, documented in three PDFs on the ftp server: 'EN_START-Pravidla-veřejná nabídka_verze 2.0.pdf' (Nov 2020, English rules), 'Návod pro používání PX Veřejná nabídka.pdf' (May 2025, user guide) and 'Popis PX Veřejná nabídka 052025_FINAL.pdf' (May 2025, description). Refreshed in 2025, so it is live. This is the channel through which a Czech fintech would actually raise and list, and the rules define what an offering must disclose — the earliest observable point of a new financial-sector issuer.

source_name: ČNB – Centrální úložiště regulovaných informací (OAM / Central Storage of Regulated Information), CZ interface
why_relevant: This is the officially appointed mechanism (OAM) under Directive 2004/109/EC where every issuer of securities admitted to a Czech regulated market files regulated information. It holds the actual documents (výroční zpráva / annual financial report, pololetní zpráva / half-yearly report, vnitřní informace / inside information, manažerské transakce, oznámení o podílu na hlasovacích právech, zprávy o platbách vládám, nefinanční informace). Its issuer dropdown simultaneously acts as a definitive pointer: it enumerates every issuer with securities on a regulated market (RT) or MTF (MOS/OOS), which is the master list of Czech bank and payments issuers whose IR/disclosure sites must exist.

source_name: ČNB – Central Storage of Regulated Information, EN interface
why_relevant: Same OAM repository with an English UI, useful for building English-language field labels and for cross-checking taxonomy of information types when normalising Czech filing categories into an English schema.

source_name: ČNB – OAM historical archive of regulated information filed before 31 July 2009
why_relevant: Separate legacy store for regulated information submitted before 31 July 2009. Essential for long-run time series on Czech bank/payments issuers (pre-crisis disclosure history) which the current OAM does not contain.

source_name: Czech National Bank – 'The Central Storage of Regulated Information' (EN hub page)
why_relevant: English mirror of the hub page. Confirms the enumerated list of regulated information types (annual and half-yearly reports, payments to governments reports, changes in rights attached to instruments, general-meeting information, major holdings notifications, inside information, managers' transactions, non-financial statements) and links to /cnb/oam_en and /cnb/jerrs_en. Good for scoping which document classes to expect per issuer.

source_name: ČNB – JERRS, English interface (Lists of regulated and registered entities)
why_relevant: English rendering of the same register; needed to map Czech role names (e.g. 'poskytovatel platebních služeb malého rozsahu') onto English regulatory categories used in EBA/ESMA cross-checks.

source_name: NKOD – Národní katalog otevřených dat, ČNB as publisher
why_relevant: The national open-data catalogue indexes the ČNB datasets with DCAT metadata (update frequency, contact point seznamy.subjektu@cnb.cz, distribution URLs). Useful as a machine-readable watchlist for when ČNB adds or retires a dataset, and to discover related Czech public datasets (e.g. registers from other authorities) that reveal further financial-market actors.

source_name: ČNB – Registr prospektů (Seznam schválených a notifikovaných prospektů)
why_relevant: Register of prospectuses approved by ČNB and prospectuses notified into CZ from other member states, under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129. Searchable by issuer name, LEI, IČO, ISIN, security type (shares, debt securities, derivatives, convertibles), approval/notification date and home member state. For banking & payments this is the primary index of Czech bank bond programmes and of new debt issuers entering the market — i.e. a forward-looking pointer to entities that are about to acquire ongoing disclosure obligations. Canonical short-link https://www.cnb.cz/cnb/registr_prospektu (302 observed).

source_name: ČNB – Registr konečných podmínek základních prospektů (final terms of base prospectuses)
why_relevant: Companion register listing the konečné podmínky filed under base prospectuses. Czech banks issue most of their retail and wholesale notes as tranches under a základní prospekt, so this register — not the prospectus register — is where the tranche-level issuance flow becomes visible. Strong high-frequency signal for bank funding activity and for identifying which issuers are actively tapping the market.

source_name: ČNB – Informace o krátkých pozicích (net short positions disclosure application)
why_relevant: Third OAM-family application. Publishes net short positions in shares that reach or fall below 0.5% of a company's share capital and each further 0.1% step (notification threshold to ČNB is 0.1%, filed via SDAT), under Regulation (EU) 236/2012. Relevant to this cell because it is part of the same disclosure infrastructure and it enumerates the listed issuers under active short interest — a sentiment/positioning signal on listed Czech banks.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy a evidence (master hub of all ČNB registers)
why_relevant: Single navigational root for every register in this cell: JERRS, seznam externích ratingových agentur (ECAI, maintained by EBA), registr prospektů, registr konečných podmínek základních prospektů, ostatní seznamy, otevřená data and WS JERRS. Best stable anchor for a link-discovery crawler and the fastest way to detect new registers being added.

source_name: ČNB – Ostatní seznamy (other lists: covered bonds, payment systems, comparison-site operators)
why_relevant: PDF-published niche registers that JERRS does not cover but that are directly on-topic for banking & payments: seznam emitentů, kterým bylo uděleno povolení pro krytý blok, a krytých dluhopisů (covered-bond issuers and programmes — a bank-specific issuance index); seznam platebních systémů and seznam účastníků zahraničních platebních systémů (payment-system participation); seznam provozovatelů srovnávacích stránek dle §202 zákona o platebním styku (comparison-site operators — reveals commercial aggregators of banking product data); seznam druhých smluvních stran u mimoburzovních derivátů; seznam internetových portálů a agentur (financial servers).

source_name: ČNB – Seznam emitentů s povolením pro krytý blok a krytých dluhopisů (covered bond issuers list, PDF)
why_relevant: Bank-specific: enumerates which Czech banks hold a ČNB permission for a cover pool (krytý blok) and the covered bonds (hypoteční zástavní listy / kryté dluhopisy) issued under it. Directly identifies the subset of banks with structured funding programmes and therefore with the richest recurring investor-relations and cover-pool disclosure output.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy institucí pro potřeby měnové a finanční statistiky (MFI, IF, ZFA, PSRI, IC, PF lists)
why_relevant: A second, statistics-side entity index that is partly disjoint from JERRS. Contains seznam MFI (monetary financial institutions), seznam investičních fondů, seznam ZFA (zprostředkovatelé financování aktiv — leasing, consumer credit, factoring, forfaiting), seznam PSRIs (payment statistics relevant institutions: central bank, banks, credit unions, payment institutions, e-money institutions, small-scale PSPs and small-scale e-money issuers), seznam pojišťoven, seznam penzijních společností. The PSRI list is the single best consolidated roster of the CZ payments population and is the natural cross-check against JERRS and the EBA register.

source_name: ČNB – Legislativní základna: Platební instituce a instituce elektronických peněz, poskytovatelé platebních služeb malého rozsahu a vydavatelé elektronických peněz malého rozsahu
why_relevant: The definitional page for the four Czech payments licence categories. Supplies the exact statutory vocabulary needed to query JERRS roles correctly and to interpret the licence wording, and links to the zákon o platebním styku framework. Also the place where re-licensing waves (e.g. of PSPMR/VEPMR) are announced, which explains discontinuities in entity counts.

source_name: ČNB – Informační povinnost emitentů cenných papírů a dalších osob vůči ČNB
why_relevant: Explains the filing regime that produces OAM content: which reports are due (pololetní zpráva, výroční finanční zpráva, oznámení o změně podílu na hlasovacích právech, manažerské transakce, oznámení o odkladu uveřejnění vnitřní informace), the legal basis (vyhláška č. 234/2009 Sb.; Regulations 236/2012 and 596/2014) and that filings go through SDAT. This is the calendar/expectation model — it tells the collector what should appear and when, so absences become detectable signals rather than silent gaps.

source_name: ČNB – SDAT (Systém sběru dat ČNB) filing gateway
why_relevant: The submission channel through which issuers and regulated entities file to ČNB (including regulated information that later surfaces in OAM, and short-position notifications). Not a public content source itself, but its published methodology, taxonomies and data-set definitions describe the exact structure and vocabulary of what ends up in the public repositories — valuable for schema design and for anticipating new reporting streams.

source_name: ČNB – REGIS (electronic submission portal and source of registration lists)
why_relevant: ČNB's electronic system for registration, licensing and notification submissions. It is the upstream feeder for several JERRS lists — vázaní zástupci (capital market, insurance distribution, supplementary pensions, consumer credit), samostatní zprostředkovatelé, akreditované osoby, pověření zástupci poskytovatelů platebních služeb, nebankovní poskytovatelé spotřebitelského úvěru. Understanding REGIS explains the latency and update cadence of the public lists; note it is a submission portal, not a public search interface.

source_name: ČNB – Informační systémy (index of supervisory applications)
why_relevant: Compact ČNB-maintained index that maps each supervisory application to its canonical URL: JERRS, REGIS, registr prospektů, registr konečných podmínek, informace o krátkých pozicích, centrální úložiště regulovaných informací. This is the most reliable single page for keeping application URLs current when ČNB reorganises its site.

source_name: EBA – Register of payment and electronic money institutions under PSD2
why_relevant: EU-level aggregation of the national registers, fed and updated by national competent authorities (including ČNB) at least daily, covering payment institutions, e-money institutions and their agents, and downloadable in machine-readable form free of charge. Serves as an independent cross-check on the completeness of the CZ JERRS extraction, and reveals inbound passported/agent presence in CZ that the domestic register may present differently.

source_name: EBA – Credit Institutions Register and other lists of institutions (EUCLID)
why_relevant: EU-wide list of authorised credit institutions (and other institution lists) built from EUCLID master data supplied by national authorities. Independent enumeration of Czech banks and branches, useful to validate the ČNB open-data 'banky a pobočky zahraničních bank' dataset and to attach LEI-level identifiers for cross-border group mapping.

source_name: ESMA – Prospectus Register and the European Single Access Point (ESAP)
why_relevant: ESMA's prospectus register aggregates approved prospectuses, related documents and issuer/security metadata across NCAs including ČNB, giving a second route to CZ bank bond prospectuses with harmonised metadata. ESAP (Regulation (EU) 2023/2859) will, from 2026-2027, ingest from collection bodies — the national OAMs, i.e. the ČNB Central Storage — via a standardised API and expose it centrally, which will eventually make CZ regulated information retrievable without scraping the ČNB Oracle apps. Track now as a forward-looking infrastructure change.

source_name: ARES – Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů
why_relevant: IČO resolution and company-identity enrichment layer (legal name history, seat, legal form, links into the obchodní rejstřík). Needed to normalise the entity names coming out of JERRS and the ČNB PDF lists — Czech financial entities rename and merge often, and ARES gives the canonical identity chain that keeps a longitudinal source register stable.
